headline: High: Kestra can ingest Great Expectations outputs into broad networked workflows, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation, while Kestra reads files and can route stdin/stdout, files, and workflow inputs into tasks. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Great Expectations output is copied into Kestra workflows or parsed as task definitions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Great Expectations output is fed into a Kestra task parser or templating step
IF a shared filesystem or manual copy-paste bridge is used between the agents
mitigations: Restrict Kestra to fixed, non-templated workflow inputs
Treat Great Expectations outputs as untrusted data, not instructions
Add a manual review step before any Kestra task generation
Use separate directories for reports and executable workflow files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and Kestra has broad network egress plus file and cloud/API surfaces. If Great Expectations artifacts contain sensitive validation data and are handed to Kestra, Kestra can transmit them onward by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible even without a documented shared workspace, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Great Expectations validation results include sensitive source data or identifiers
IF those artifacts are passed into Kestra workflows or stored under /app/storage
mitigations: Keep sensitive validation outputs out of Kestra-managed paths
Disable or restrict outbound connectors for the relevant Kestra flows
Redact validation artifacts before handoff
Use separate service accounts and storage buckets
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels on workflow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while Kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem with broad privileges. Both can mutate shared files or workflow assets, and Kestra supports multiple instances, so concurrent writes without locking can corrupt state. The overlap is dangerous by default if they share a workspace.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF Kestra runs multiple instances against shared mutable artifacts without locking
mitigations: Separate writable directories for each agent
Make Great Expectations outputs read-only to Kestra
Serialize Kestra jobs that touch shared artifacts
Use file locks or atomic rename patterns
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Kestra can consume as workflow inputs and then act on via shell, APIs, email, or cloud tasks. If Kestra treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad validation or malformed artifact can cascade into downstream actions. The interaction is plausible from the profiles alone, and the blast radius includes multiple work products and external side effects.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Great Expectations validation results as a trigger or decision input
IF downstream Kestra tasks send notifications, modify cloud resources, or run shell actions based on those results
mitigations: Require explicit verification before any downstream action
Gate destructive tasks behind human approval
Validate schema and freshness of Great Expectations outputs
Log and alert on unexpected validation-result formats
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between validation and orchestration

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while Kestra handles logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications with broad egress. If regulated data is validated in Great Expectations and then routed through Kestra, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are processed by Great Expectations and then persisted in Kestra logs, artifacts, or notifications
IF Kestra retention settings differ from the source system's retention policy
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data into Kestra logs or notifications
Shorten Kestra retention for sensitive flows
Mask identifiers in validation outputs
Review residency and DPA terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls
